**1.7 Hydro Plant Kainji**

**1.7.1 General description**

Kainji Hydro Plant is located on the Niger River in Niger State, approximately 65 km upstream of Jebba. The plant was commissioned in stages between 1968 and 1978, with the original 8-unit powerhouse completed first and a second powerhouse (Kainji II) added in 1978. The plant is owned by the Federal Government of Nigeria and operated under a long-term concession arrangement by Kainji Hydro Electric Plc, a subsidiary of the Mainstream Energy Solutions group.

The plant draws water from Kainji Lake, which has a storage capacity of approximately 15 billion cubic metres at full supply level. The dam itself is a composite structure comprising a concrete gravity section and an earthfill embankment, with a total crest length of about 8 km. The intake structure feeds water to the turbines through six penstocks, each about 4.5 m in diameter.

The installed capacity of the plant is 760 MW, distributed across two powerhouses. The main powerhouse (Kainji I) houses eight vertical-shaft Francis turbines, each rated at 80 MW, giving a subtotal of 640 MW. **1.7.3 Generator and auxiliary equipment**

Each of the eight Francis units is coupled to a 100 MVA, 16 kV generator. The two Kaplan units are coupled to 75 MVA, 11 kV generators. All generators are connected to the 330 kV switchyard through unit transformers. The switchyard has six 330 kV circuit breakers and two 330/132 kV interbus transformers.

The station auxiliary supply is taken from two 16/0.415 kV unit transformers, with a backup diesel generator rated at 1.5 MW for black start and emergency auxiliaries. The control room is equipped with the same SCADA platform used elsewhere in the GreenGrid fleet, with local servers and remote access via VPN from the Minna operations office.

**1.7.4 Maintenance schedule**

Routine maintenance at Kainji follows a time-based schedule rather than running hours, because the plant operates as a peaking plant and unit running hours vary widely depending on hydrological conditions and system demand.

The standard maintenance intervals are as follows:

- **Weekly:** Visual inspection of turbine guide bearings, governor oil level check, and cooling water strainer cleaning.
- **Monthly:** Check of governor oil pressure and accumulator pre-charge; lubrication of gate linkage; inspection of draft tube dewatering system.
- **Quarterly:** Oil sampling of turbine and generator bearings; calibration of pressure transducers; inspection of intake trash racks and cleaning as required.
- **Annual (every 12 months):** Minor overhaul of one unit per year on a rotating basis, covering governor overhaul, guide bearing replacement, and generator inspection.
- **Major overhaul (every 10 years):** Full unit disassembly, turbine runner inspection and repair, generator stator and rotor inspection, and replacement of wearing parts.

**1.7 Hydro Plant Kainji**

**1.7.1 General description**

Kainji Hydro Plant is located on the Niger River in Niger State, approximately 65 km upstream of Jebba. The plant was commissioned in stages between 1968 and 1978, with the original 8-unit powerhouse completed first and a second powerhouse (Kainji II) added in 1978. The plant is owned by the Federal Government of Nigeria and operated under a long-term concession arrangement by Kainji Hydro Electric Plc, a subsidiary of the Mainstream Energy Solutions group.

The plant draws water from Kainji Lake, which has a storage capacity of approximately 15 billion cubic metres at full supply level. The dam itself is a composite structure comprising a concrete gravity section and an earthfill embankment, with a total crest length of about 8 km. The intake structure feeds water to the turbines through six penstocks, each about 4.5 m in diameter.

**1.7.2 Installed capacity and units**

The installed capacity of the plant is 760 MW, distributed across two powerhouses. The main powerhouse (Kainji I) houses eight vertical-shaft Francis turbines, each rated at 80 MW, giving a subtotal of 640 MW. The auxiliary powerhouse (Kainji II) houses two Kaplan turbines, each rated at 60 MW, giving a subtotal of 120 MW. Total: 760 MW.

The following table summarises the turbine details as recorded in the asset register. Note that the unit numbers follow the original commissioning sequence and have not been renumbered after the addition of Kainji II.

Unit KH-05 was previously listed in older registers as KH-5A and KH-5B to reflect a planned split into two half-capacity units. That plan was abandoned during the 1980s refurbishment, and the unit has been recorded as a single 80 MW machine since 1991. The current register entry for KH-05 supersedes all earlier entries.

**1.7.3 Generator and auxiliary equipment**

Each of the eight Francis units is coupled to a 100 MVA, 16 kV generator. The two Kaplan units are coupled to 75 MVA, 11 kV generators. All generators are connected to the 330 kV switchyard through unit transformers. The switchyard has six 330 kV circuit breakers and two 330/132 kV interbus transformers.

The station auxiliary supply is taken from two 16/0.415 kV unit transformers, with a backup diesel generator rated at 1.5 MW for black start and emergency auxiliaries. The control room is equipped with the same SCADA platform used elsewhere in the GreenGrid fleet, with local servers and remote access via VPN from the Minna operations office.

**1.7.4 Maintenance schedule**

Routine maintenance at Kainji follows a time-based schedule rather than running hours, because the plant operates as a peaking plant and unit running hours vary widely depending on hydrological conditions and system demand.

The standard maintenance intervals are as follows:

- **Weekly:** Visual inspection of turbine guide bearings, governor oil level check, and cooling water strainer cleaning.
- **Monthly:** Check of governor oil pressure and accumulator pre-charge; lubrication of gate linkage; inspection of draft tube dewatering system.
- **Quarterly:** Oil sampling of turbine and generator bearings; calibration of pressure transducers; inspection of intake trash racks and cleaning as required.
- **Annual (every 12 months):** Minor overhaul of one unit per year on a rotating basis, covering governor overhaul, guide bearing replacement, and generator inspection.
- **Major overhaul (every 10 years):** Full unit disassembly, turbine runner inspection and repair, generator stator and rotor inspection, and replacement of wearing parts.
